correctness.rationale: For any \(m\ge3\), a connected bipartite \(2m\)-vertex graph with \(m\) domatic classes has no universal vertex (otherwise it is a star with domatic number 2), hence each of its m classes must have size exactly two. A same-side pair would equal that entire side and strand at least four vertices of the other side, contradicting domination by remaining pairs. Every class is therefore a cross-pair, so the sides have size m. Each selected cross-pair must dominate every other vertex on both sides, forcing all off-diagonal cross-edges; missing edges form a matching. Conversely each canonical pair in \(\(K_{m,m}\)-M_t\) dominates, \(\gamma=2\) and \(d=m\). Every deleted edge forces its two endpoints to be paired, leaving \((m-t)!\) bijections on unmatched vertices. If \(t<m\) a further diagonal deletion preserves \(d=m\); if \(t=m\) an offdiagonal deletion destroys the matching-of-missing-edges condition and forces d<m, with d>=m-1 by merging the two affected domatic classes. All quantifiers, \(m\ge3\) boundary, connectedness, distinct meanings of domination and domatic criticality were rechecked. An independent standard-library verifier exhausts all 800 and 102528 bipartite-side graphs on six and eight vertices and pairing counts for \(3\le m\le5\); this is supplementary and not used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The proof yields a complete iff structural characterization of the bipartite, \(\gamma=2\) subclass of Matsumoto's explicit Problem 5.2, plus all optimum-partition counts and the exact edge-critical member. Matsumoto explicitly treats \(K_{n,n}\) and a one-edge-deleted example, without deriving the stated necessary condition or enumeration; Spakowski classifies the computational difficulty of criticality, not these bipartite extremizers. Mathematical-record index results closest by graph or name concern other domination variants and do not imply the domatic theorem. Thus no equivalent or stronger covering result was found in reviewed sources, while acknowledging residual priority uncertainty.

value.rationale: The theorem completely solves a natural bipartite subclass of the explicit domination-number-two domatically-perfect characterization problem (Matsumoto 2020, Problem 5.2), rather than giving another isolated computed parameter. It classifies every permissible graph, counts all optimal resource-group partitions, and determines exactly which classified graph is sensitive to every edge deletion. The counting and crown criticality follow from a structural rigidity condition forced by the extremal domatic coloring; no arbitrary finite parameter slice or routine numerical bound is used. Scope is properly restricted to simple connected bipartite order 2m>=6.
